title: Prophetic Symbolism and Shifts in Person
english: "He gave us for hunting to those walking their paths." Zachariah 11:10–11: "And I will take my good staff, and I will cast it away to scatter my covenant, which I had distributed to all the peoples; and it shall be scattered in that day, and the Canaanites shall know the sheep being guarded, because it is the word of the Lord."

Because the people of circumcision were abandoned by the shepherd due to their unfaithfulness toward him, the lying ones encountered [the consequences], as if the dying were dying and the vanishing were vanishing, and the remnants were turned to eat the flesh of their neighbor.

A calling occurs of the Church from the nations having believed in Christ, which he also named a praiseworthy staff, that is, a kingdom, saying: "And I will take the good staff." But this surpassed what the Father said to the Son: "Ask from me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance."

Because the royal scepter was cast away by the one having taken all the nations as inheritance, the covenant toward all the peoples was scattered, concerning which it is said in Deuteronomy in a great song in this manner: "When the Most High divided the nations, as he scattered the sons of Adam, he set the boundaries of the nations according to the number of the angels of God." This covenant having been scattered by Christ, the angels no longer presiding over the nations, an inheritance and a portion has become all the nations of the one who cast away the good staff upon the dissolution of the covenant toward all the peoples.

And this excellence is perfected in that day prepared by the sun of righteousness, which Abraham, the father of all the nations of the believers, rejoiced to see, having been blessed in his seed, all those of the nations fulfilling [the promise], men having their faith reckoned as righteousness.

Concerning this day, the whole choir of holy men and angels sings and declares: "This is the day which the Lord made; let us rejoice and be glad in it" (Ps 118:24), being sons of those to whom the Savior said: "You are the light of the world" (Matt 5:14). "The day has approached, that we may walk decorously as in a day."
Having endured these divine exploits, the Canaanites shall know, being sheep being guarded, "that it is the word of the Lord" regarding the lying ones...

Being a signifier of great and exceeding mysteries, which it is necessary to understand, [it is] both a rod and a covenant toward all the peoples. 4.112 The Canaanites were being called out from the nations, prepared to become the inheritance of the Son of God, through which they had blindness regarding what was spoken: 'Learn from me that I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls' (Matt 11:29).

4.113 Zach. XI, 12–13: 'And I will say to them: If it is good in your sight, give, having stood my wages, or refuse; and they stood my wages, thirty pieces of silver. And the Lord said to me: Cast them into the potter's house, and consider if it is tested, in the manner in which I was tested against them. And they took the thirty pieces of silver, and threw them into the house of the Lord into the potter's house.'

4.114 The prophetic words, being uttered enigmatically, abruptly change the persons of those speaking and of whom they speak; and indeed, from many utterances, it is possible to believe and to demonstrate the doctrine. But in order not to mishear the word, one must take from Jeremiah, spoken in the presence of God, thus: 'Run to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem and see if there is anyone doing faithfulness and mercy' (Jer 3:4), or 'judgment' as some of the manuscripts have, 'and I said: As the Lord lives, they say; therefore they do not swear upon a lie.'

4.115 For having God spoken to the holy men: 'Run to and fro through the squares of Jerusalem and see if there is anyone in it doing these things,' those having received the command answer: 'As the Lord lives, they say'; toward whom God says: 'Therefore they do not swear upon a lie.' See how many changes of persons are brought about in these few symbols, not being dispersed according to the letter but in the understanding.

4.116 Just as it is regarding the received testimony, so it is in the voice of Zechariah having been set forth. For the Savior having said—for He himself is the one announcing the things set before regarding the rejection of those of the circumcision—and having announced furthermore regarding the calling of the nations who formerly were idolaters, He says from another beginning: 'I was answered and I said to them,' that is, to the Jews: 'If it is good and just in your sight, give, that is to say, having determined, my wages; but if not, refuse, declining...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Deceitful Wages and False Doctrines
english: My words. For those who agreed that my wages were thirty pieces of silver. It is appropriate to receive both a wage and silver. Often, the divine teachings and the word are signified by this name: 'The words of the Lord are pure words, like silver refined in a furnace, tested, cleansed in the earth seven times' (Ps 12:6). And again, it is said proverbially: 'The tongue of the righteous is like refined silver' (Prov 10:20). For the word is signified by the name of the tongue.

And since not all silver mentioned allegorically is praised, but some is also reproached, thus God says to the false teachers of Israel: 'Your silver is worthless' (Jer 6:30); He does not mean a physical coin, but a deceitful word. And regarding those who use it to describe the discerning ones, to say of the generation producing these things: 'Call them rejected silver, for the Lord has rejected them,' it is manifest that they are deceitful and forbidden things.

This understanding is the proverbial ordinance brought forth thus: 'Silver given with deceit should be regarded as shards.' For the deceptive and contentious word brought forth with deceit by sophists—even if it seems to be about great things, the so-called 'exaltations, puffed up according to the knowledge of God'—is to be announced as being to be regarded as shards; such are those who are described as 'those who set their minds on earthly things' (Col 3:2), whom Isaiah said are 'those shouting from the earth' (Isa 28:9).

Since there is indeed a difference between logical silvers, having established the wage of those of the circumcision against those who toil over them as thirty pieces of silver, the Father says to the one having received the thirty pieces of silver: 'Cast them into the treasury and test if it is worthy' (Matt 27:5), the silver given, 'in the manner in which I was tested' on their behalf. For thus it will be revealed whether I am providing worthily the wage for which I accepted toil on their behalf, 'laying down my life and giving it as a ransom for many' (Mk 10:45).

Having said these things of the Father, I say this: Cast the thirty pieces of silver into the treasury, the one 'having become obedient unto death' (Phil 2:8) without hesitation, following what was commanded; they took, He says, the silver and threw it into the house of the Lord into the treasury (Matt 27:5). When this was fulfilled, it became known of the Pharisees and the others from...
The reward of circumcision is deceitful, just as those searching the scriptures which testify concerning the Savior as he spoke them have considered it to be a counterfeit coin.

For often in the Gospels the wicked word of those being accused is exposed, as in: 'This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me; and in vain they worship me, teaching commandments of men as doctrines' (Matt 15:8), nullifying the commandment of God through their harmful tradition. Likewise, those proposing an unproven word concerning whether it is necessary to give tribute to Caesar or not are exposed, as they themselves were accused of being deceitful and speaking with much cunning from that very moment; for when being asked, the Savior said: 'Show me the coin' (Matt 22:19), meaning 'whose image and inscription it has.' And those saying: 'Caesar's,' were strongly rebated upon hearing: 'Therefore render to Caesar the things of Caesar, and to God the things of God' (Matt 22:21).

And not only do the Jews approaching the Savior in a testing manner possess an unproven word, but also the heretics in Christianity who pseudo-doctrinalize, 'walking in cunning and deceiving the word of the Lord,' diverting and distorting the will of the God-breathed oracles; whom one must also reject, considering their deceitful word to be as counterfeit silver. Is the word of those setting two unbegotten principles, good and evil—and these are Manichaeans—not unproven? And [is it not unproven] of those saying the Son is a creature and dividing the Holy Spirit from Father and Son? And [is it not unproven] of the impious ones regarding the incarnation of the Savior, those thinking the Savior appeared and was not true?

Not only is the counterfeit silver made manifest from the crucible of the house of God, but also the genuine [silver] bearing the image and character of the All-King Savior, 'having been purified sevenfold,' which must be held and in which one must prosper by possession. They are grasping that those whom Judas received, thirty pieces of silver from the Jews in order that he might betray the Lord (Matt 26:15), are signified also from the spoken word, and [this is] the greatest indictment of the Jews who gave and of Judas who received the thirty pieces of silver for betrayal. For it was necessary for them a reward...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Restoration of the Divided Kingdoms
english: to provide to the one who labored for the salvation of them and of the whole cosmos, but not so that 'the one who vivifies all things' might be denied.

4.128 It is necessary to cast the blasphemies, which the Jews bring against the Savior crucified for the sake of the whole creation, into the house of the God-breathed writings and into the vessel contained therein, so that they may be convicted of being unheeding, rather than opposing the prophecies concerning Christ and his cross.
4.129 Zach. XI, 14: And he cast away the second rod, the staff, to scatter the covenant between Judah and between Israel.

4.130 Our Savior and Lord has taken two rods, the beauty of which he first summoned, having previously cast away that called beauty, revealing the mysteries already made clear; now, having cast away the one called the staff, he scattered the covenant between Israel and Judah.

4.131 What is the staff called the staff? From the great song it is again to be learned. And the things of the song are held thus, as they were previously set forth: 'When the Most High divided the nations, as he scattered the sons of Adam, he set boundaries of nations according to the number of the angels of God, and there became a divided people of the Lord, his Jacob, a staff of inheritance, his Israel.' These things are said concerning the whole nation of the Hebrews being one rod and one portion. And for a long time the whole nation remained unsuitably acting as one rod, according to that which is proclaimed in the Psalms to the King and Forethinker of all: 'Remember your assembly, which I will gather from the beginning; I will redeem the rod of your inheritance.'

4.132 This one kingdom was divided into two leaderships, as Judah is called, and Ephraim, with those remaining in Jerusalem having the succession under the house of David from the tribe of Judah, and those having descended into Samaria having Jeroboam as leader, having sinned against Israel, being from the tribe of Ephraim.

4.133 And for a long time the wickedness of the division remained, with the king of Judah and the tyrant of Samaria apostatizing and contending against one another, until God may have mercy, and again show the twelve tribes as one kingdom, with only Judah holding as...

Concerning this restoration, it is brought forth in Hosea the prophet, the All-King saying: 'The sons of Israel and the sons of Judah shall be gathered, and they shall set for themselves one beginning and shall ascend from the land, because great is the day of Jezreel' (Hosea 2:23).

One must attend to the prophecy declaring that those being restored into one kingdom ascend from the land, making it clear that they exist down in the land, having been scattered by their own division away from the single hegemony. After the covenant of the schism having worked in the midst of Judah and Israel for a time, a scattering and a resolution of it occurs by the grace of the Savior, so that from the departure of the difference of the schisms, the so-called splintered rod might become one under a single king as before, he having the succession from Judah, so that there might be one flock and one shepherd existing under the lawful king of the whole nation.

Concerning such a restoration of the two kingdoms into one lawful beginning, it is brought forth in the prophet Ezekiel; and thus the prophetic voice has: 'And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, take for yourself a rod and write upon it Judah and the sons of Israel lying near to it; and a second rod you shall take for yourself and write it: To Joseph, the rod of Ephraim and all the sons of Israel placed toward him. And you shall join them to one another to yourself into one rod to bind them, and they shall be in your hand' (Ezekiel 10:9-11).

And it shall be when they say to you, sons of your people, saying: 'Do you not announce to us what these things are to you?' (Ezekiel 11:17). And you shall say to them: 'Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I will take the tribe of Joseph through the hand of Ephraim and the tribes of Israel lying near to him, and I will give them upon the tribe of Judah; and the rods shall be upon which you have written them in your hand before them, and you shall say to them: 'Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I take the whole house of Israel from the midst of the nations, where they entered there and were, and I will gather them from all those around them and I will bring them into the land of Israel; and I will give them into one nation in my land and in the mountains of Israel' (Ezekiel 11:14-16).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
